note: The original says the house shed. The rewrite says it was stripped and drops the game term shed. Keep the game word shed. It is a term in this game.
last: The house was stripped in spring. We moved into the hollow shell. // The new one is off being a house somewhere else.

note: The original says she caught the hare's cast. The rewrite says she found it and drops the game term catch. Keep the game word catch. It is a term in this game.
last: I found a hare's cast! The real hare is still out there, though. It's much faster than this.

note: Keep every direction exactly as the original says it.
last: Knuckle always switches when things go south. I don't. I stay loyal.

note: The original says Rib lies west along the Midden Road. The rewrite says to start at Rib and then head west, which changes the direction.
last: Tell the Sealkeepers. Start with Rib, then head west on the Midden Road.

note: The original says the fracture has come right up to the door. The rewrite says trouble has arrived and drops the game term fracture. Keep the game word fracture. It is a term in this game.
last: Tell my little turnip that trouble has finally arrived at the doorstep.

note: The original asks Ouro to move one step over to the side. The rewrite says one step back.
last: Uh, take 1 step back? It's going to come off at an angle.

note: The original says the whorl picked Ouro back in return. The rewrite says it chose Ouro again.
last: Look at that. It's chosen you again. That bit's on the house.

note: The original jokes that holding the Register costs a cowrie. The rewrite says storage costs a cowrie, which reads as a rule about the Midden.
last: Here's the Register. You catch a species, I log it. Writing is free. Storage costs a cowrie.

note: The original says a weaker whorl makes a surer catch. The rewrite says less strength means better control, which changes the catch rule.
last: Dull them down a bit, then catch them. Less strength means better control. // Weak enough, and it's foolproof.

note: The original prices Knuckle's hands at a house each and calls the pearl cheap. The rewrite prices each pearl at a house and then calls the pearl cheap, which contradicts itself.
last: Start with the Rib. Knuckle holds it steady. Hands-on Knuckle? I'd ask a house per pearl. // The pearl itself is cheap.

note: The original says the Hermits take (seize) big whorls. The rewrite says they bring them.
last: Large whorls can wrench a Seal loose. That's why we bring large whorls.

note: The original says he will go and wait by the well. The rewrite says he will stay where he is.
last: The well stays dry until she returns. I'll stay here and wait.

note: The original means the pearl Knuckle gives out. The rewrite turns the name into a "knuckle-pearl".
last: You've got a knuckle-pearl, right? Then you need one of these.

note: The original notice names Ouro. The rewrite switches to "You acquire", unlike every other notice. Keep the name Ouro.
last: You acquire the prising iron.

note: Keep every direction exactly as the original says it.
last: Anyway, next stop is Mast. Head west along the Dry Sea.

note: The original hands over the Rib pearl. The rewrite addresses Ouro as "Rib".
last: Here you go, Rib. The pearl is yours.

note: The original says you get tide from the small moves. The rewrite says from "subtle shifts", which no longer names the moves.
last: Crests require tide, right? You gain tide from the subtle shifts. That's the entire mechanism.

note: The original says Leeward is one keeper against eleven Hermits. The rewrite says Leeward has one keeper.
last: Leeward has 1 keeper and there are 11 of them. So I'm gonna help. After I beat you.

note: The original greets Ouro as a late one. The rewrite says latecomer, which means someone who arrived late.
last: GREETINGS, latecomer!! Clear skies overhead. Conditions are favorable for a trial.

note: The original has nacre caught in the drift. The rewrite says mother-of-pearl and drops the game term nacre. Keep the game word catch, nacre. It is a term in this game.
last: On the distant islet, a pile of driftwood tangled with mother-of-pearl.

note: Keep every direction exactly as the original says it.
last: On the western islet, a reed plug trimmed for a bell, left unused.

note: The original says Grandad shed in the nave. The rewrite says he was buried there. Keep the game word shed. It is a term in this game.
last: My grandfather was buried in the nave, // and his cast has been singing the same song there for sixty years.

note: The original means stop the wind-up or take the hit. The rewrite turns it into a threat and loses the battle advice.
last: hear that? yeah, that's a wind-up. cut it out, or you're gonna pay for it.

note: The original has a notion under the acorns. The rewrite says a secret and drops the game term notion. Keep the game word notion. It is a term in this game.
last: Past the sleeping stump in the hollow lies a heap of acorns with a secret hidden beneath them.

note: The original says two nacre. The rewrite says two shells and drops the game term nacre. Keep the game word nacre. It is a term in this game.
last: Beyond the sleeping howl in the dell, two shells wrapped in moss.

note: The original says rain falls upward near the Bole and carries hats up. The rewrite says the rain is strong and loses the upward rain the next line depends on.
last: Keep your hat low near the Bole. The rain there is strong enough to strip it off.

note: The original is about a furnace cast. The rewrite drops cast and says a furnace. Keep the game word cast. It is a term in this game.
last: A furnace stays warm for a century. I sleep right against it. Best sleep of my life.

note: The original says arms in first. The rewrite says arms out first.
last: Arms out first. Then the head. That's it.

note: The original says the Tusk should come out easily. The rewrite says the Hermits should take it easy.
last: We're undermining the Tusk. The oldest one there is. Should take it easy. Probably.

note: Keep the game word charm. It is a term in this game.
last: (Press X, select Charm, and equip a pearl. Charms provide benefits to your entire team in battle.)

note: Keep every direction exactly as the original says it.
last: The Hilt road lies to the east, and the Shingle to the southeast. // Amber wishes to see you before anything else.

note: The original says the late ones (people whose shell has not come off) should get a go. The rewrite says those who came in late.
last: She says those who came in late deserve a turn. Here. Your turn.

note: The original says she shed the day she climbed down. The rewrite says she took it off and drops the game term shed. Keep the game word shed. It is a term in this game.
last: It's a Rider's cast, passed down from my grandmother's grandmother. // She took it off the very day she climbed down.

note: The original says the cast never fought. The rewrite says it never resisted.
last: It never resisted. It had walked a long way. It always wanted to go north.

note: Keep every direction exactly as the original says it.
last: The glass road lies to the southeast. The rule is the same. Secure the sword before the glass. // Quillon is quite adamant about this.

note: The choice to catch the moon with a horn becomes "Grab it" and drops the game term catch.
last: Grab it

note: The original says she said a new one. The rewrite says she said there is a new one.
last: Tell my little turnip she said there's a new one.

note: The original says Ouro lit the glass room. The rewrite says Ouro shattered it.
last: You shattered the glass room! I heard it all the way from here.

note: The original says every Hand wears her glove and she has never shaken one. The rewrite says she gloves every hand and none are shaken, which is garbled.
last: I glove every hand. None are shaken. It's sad.

note: The original says nobody drew the Blank into the map. The rewrite says nobody summoned it.
last: No one summoned me. Thus, I remain where I please. Today, that is here.

note: The original says the shell copies Ouro's steps the wrong way round. The rewrite says mirrors them but in reverse, which can read as the same way round and muddles the puzzle hint.
last: Old Amber's first shell mirrors each of Ouro's steps, but in reverse.

note: The leading comma becomes the literal text "[comma]".
last: [comma] hole filled

note: The original tells the turnip about soup. The rewrite sends love to "my little turnip soup".
last: Give my love to my little turnip soup.

note: Keep the name Sunday.
last: Tell them she's to be brought home on Sundays. Every single one.

note: The original means come home on Sundays without exception. The rewrite says it's Sunday. Keep the name Sundays.
last: Tell my little turnip it's Sunday, without fail.

note: Keep every direction exactly as the original says it.
last: Reach the eastern edge of the Margin.

note: The original asks who is turning Ouro's post. The rewrite asks who is keeping watch at it.
last: Stay seated for a minute before you leave. Who's keeping watch at your post while you're away?

note: The original says a still shell is gone when the shadow passes. The rewrite says when its own shadow passes, which changes the rule.
last: (At low water, a shell that appears empty vanishes as its shadow passes.)

note: The original letter is addressed to the inside of the Volute. The rewrite says "Dear reader" and loses who she writes to.
last: Dear reader. Another one washed ashore today, hidden beneath a crab. The crab says hello.

note: The original says the family is inside the whelk because it is low water. The rewrite says they are good to go and loses that they are inside.
last: The tide is low, so we're good to go. Hi! No stopping now.

note: Keep the words written in capitals exactly as they are.
last: I'm rocking, Dad.

note: The original says the writer is nobody here. The rewrite says nobody here knows them.
last: Dear whoever writes these. No one here knows them. We checked. Your letters are so huge.

note: The original says the Strandmonger keeps a shop counter in the east petal. The rewrite says he tracks a counter. Keep every direction exactly as the original says it.
last: The Strandmonger tracks a counter located in the eastern petal.

note: The original warns against breaking the Sand Dollar to get at the doves. The rewrite says break the bank.
last: There are five doves down in the town square. Don't break the bank trying to catch them. // Folks have already tried.

note: The original says they came off the old shell. The rewrite says they arrived on it.
last: Our ancestors arrived on an old shell five generations ago. We walked the entire distance. // My feet still ache from it.

note: The original says your trader, meaning Ouro's Strandmonger. The rewrite says our trader.
last: Our trader buys our cowrie shells by the sack. We simply sweep them off the seaweed. // It's the easiest money you'll ever make.

note: Keep the game word low or high water. It is a term in this game.
last: Don't sit still in a hollow shell when the tide is out. Obviously. Even the babies know that.

note: Keep the words written in capitals exactly as they are.
last: Everyone, stamp your feet!

note: Keep the game word low or high water. It is a term in this game.
last: Swim back across the Flats to the Sand Dollar at high tide.

note: The original says pull the plug from the vent. The rewrite says disconnect the vent, which can read as closing it.
last: Disconnect vent {#1}

note: The original says plug the vent. The rewrite says connect the vent, which can read as opening it.
last: Connect vent {#1} ({#2} remaining)

note: The original says to sound the vents in that order. The rewrite says to chant the sequence.
last: The notches read four, two, four, one, four. Chant that sequence, and the tip will open.

note: Keep every direction exactly as the original says it.
last: Further down the shore, a line of hollows extends to the sea, // then curves eastward along the low-water mark.

note: The original says they will climb every low water. The rewrite says every rise.
last: Here. We have arrived. We are at the edge now, exactly where the Gleaner walks. // We will climb every single rise.

note: The original says how far out the next low goes, and the rewrite says when the low tide occurs.
last: The next low tide occurs at {#1}{#2}.{walk}

note: The original says only Siphon (the character) opens the hood, and the rewrite says the Siphon as if it were an object.
last: The hood's locked tight during the low tide. Only the Siphon can open it. Sorry.

note: The original says they build a new wall behind them and move up a room, and the rewrite drops the wall building that explains the sealed old rooms.
last: We shift rooms every few years. Moving day is the best part.

note: The original says someone sealed in room five comes out at spring high, and the rewrite garbles it into Seal five for spring and drops spring from the high tide.
last: Seal five for spring? He's out at high tide. Bring hot soup.

note: The original says each mark has one to four notches, and the rewrite says one to four per row.
last: Rows of notched marks, one to four per row, spiral upward around the wall.

note: Keep the game word low or high water. It is a term in this game.
last: At high tide, this was my grandmother's, most cherishedly. // At low tide, it is yours, most deservedly.

note: Keep the game word low or high water. It is a term in this game.
last: At some high tide, a pot struck the wall with such force that six marks were scraped clean off!! // A calamitous pot.

note: The original reads marks that were cut fresh and a blank place for the next, and the rewrite turns the reading into instructions to mark and cut.
last: Then mark one, two, three, and cut new. Leave space for the next cycle.

note: The original reads that some marks were scraped off, and the rewrite tells the player to scrape them clean.
last: Newest by the point, oldest first: two notches. Scrape clean. One. Two. Scrape clean.

note: The original reads that a mark was scraped off, and the rewrite tells the player to scrape it clean.
last: Four, and a star. Scrape clean. Three. Two. One.

note: The original says three places are scraped smooth, and the rewrite tells the player to smooth out three old marks.
last: Then smooth out three old marks.

note: The original says the shut one was soft after it last shed and something reached in, and the rewrite says the low tide was soft and crept in.
last: After the shut one made the last shed, the low tide was soft. It crept in.

note: The original says it has walked with one hand ever since, and the rewrite says it has kept that hand.
last: After that low, it moved with one hand. It has kept that hand ever since.

note: The original says the hand lifts the Volute (the world), and the rewrite says a Volute as if it were an ordinary object.
last: High along the shore, a hand pulls a Volute from the sand.

note: Keep every direction exactly as the original says it.
last: Follow the footprints eastward, keeping to the upper beach.

note: The original cheers the big low (the spring low), and the rewrite says a low horizon.
last: Look at that low horizon! Once a year, you get to chase right behind the stars! Move it, move it!

note: The original says the label is driftwood with letters that grow toward the end, and the rewrite says driftwood is pressed against a marker and the letters stretch toward the bottom.
last: A marker planted in the dune, with driftwood pressed against it. // The large letters slant and stretch toward the bottom.

note: The original finds a nautilus horn and a notion (held item), and the rewrite finds a horn and an idea. Keep the game word notion. It is a term in this game.
last: Tucked into the lee of a dune, sheltered from the wind, lies a nautilus horn and an idea.

note: The original means the Mudlark does not usually lose this game, and the rewrite says it does not usually lose track of that one.
last: Huh. I don't usually lose track of that one. But I don't mind. Not really.

note: The original says Cinch wants to see it after the sea has been in, and the rewrite says once the sea has receded, which is the opposite tide.
last: (This is the old Apex. Cinch would want to see it once the sea has receded.)

note: Keep every direction exactly as the original says it.
last: Something shifts inside one of the small shells at the northern edge of the Tray.

note: The original says the key opens the last room in the Hollow Top, and the rewrite says the top shelf.
last: Here. I don't hang onto keys I can't use. This one opens the last room on the top shelf.

note: The original says the star shines across to the far knuckle (a place), and the rewrite says your farthest knuckle.
last: When a star falls at night, its light stretches all the way to your farthest knuckle. All the way!

note: The original dives into the conch's mouth at low while the Gleaner is out walking, and the rewrite dives into their mouths when they walk and drops the low tide.
last: I dive into their mouths when they walk. Big pink pearls inside!

note: The original says brushing against a wall makes it ring and the sea washes you back, and the rewrite says to tap a wall and the sea washes you away.
last: (Tap a wall to make it chime. At high tide, three chimes will summon the sea to wash you away.)

note: The original says it turns over in the great hand, and the rewrite says it flips over in your palm.
last: It flips over in your palm. ... One time.

note: The rewrite inserts a bracketed editor note [boot] into the spoken line.
last: That's my left [boot].

note: The original goal says the Strand stays open, and the rewrite tells the player to keep it open.
last: Keep the Strand open, whether through the Margin or the gray expanse of the Shoreline.

note: The original says the world has a hand in it lying palm up, and the rewrite reads it as the idiom has a hand in this.
last: Sit down. Your world has a hand in this, lying palm-up. // I once sat on its thumb for a whole afternoon.

note: The original says Wade is a small person's name, and the rewrite says it is a common word and not a person's name.
last: Sit down. Wade. That's a common word, not a person's name.

note: The original says the shell stays (is not taken) because a whorl moves in it, and the rewrite says the shell remains stationary.
last: (You can leave a whorl behind in a shell. Since the whorl is mobile, the shell remains stationary.)

note: The original says the horn is for catching a weak wild whorl, and the rewrite says capturing a faint one, which reads as knocked out. Keep the game word catch. It is a term in this game.
last: {#1} {#2}{#3}, useful for capturing a faint, wild whorl.

note: The original reward is a notion (held item), and the rewrite calls it a thought. Keep the game word notion. It is a term in this game.
last: A thought: {#1}.{#2}

note: The original says any grotto will layer the nacre on, and the rewrite tells the player to apply the nacre to a grotto.
last: {r.tan} nacre. apply this to any grotto.

note: The original says the roster shows which whorl breaks which rule, and the rewrite says which whorl counters what.
last: Include one legendary, at most. No charms. // Check the roster in the menu to see which whorl counters what.

note: The original says four working runs make it a trade (a craft), and the rewrite says that's a deal.
last: Just one set! A machine that functions once is luck. Yours ran four times. That's a deal.

note: Keep the words written in capitals exactly as they are.
last: Every single sketch set. I have nothing left to teach you, which feels incredibly strange!!

note: The original says Bezel set the ring at the player's age, and the rewrite says when you were my age.
last: Take this ring. I set it when you were my age, and it hasn't fit a single finger since.

note: The rewrite drops fine from the first sentence, so the correction about Fine has nothing to refer to. Keep the words written in capitals exactly as they are.
last: What a lovely afternoon for setting stones. I mean, splendid. "Fine" is two steps below "splendid.

note: The original asks the player to set the sketches they find and bring them back, and the rewrite asks for sketches that are already set.
last: Sketches drift through the Volute like leaves. // If you find any that are set, bring them back to me, I'd be delighted.

note: The rewrite says Slow affects the next three turns, and the original gives no count.
last: Slow. The whorl's next three turns are delayed by 30% of a turn.

note: The rewrite says Haste affects the next three turns, and the original gives no count.
last: Haste. The whorl's next three turns occur 30% of a turn earlier.

note: Keep the game word conjoin. It is a term in this game.
last: Approximately 1 in {STARBORN_ODDS} wild whorls is Starborn. Conjoined whorls can also be Starborn at the same rate.

note: Keep the game word conjoin. It is a term in this game.
last: Conjoining a Starborn whorl does not pass on its appearance.

note: The original says Shellwrights sell the harder sketches, and the rewrite says they purchase them.
last: Shellwrights purchase higher-tier sketches at the counter. Towns sell their own sketches as well as those from previous towns.

note: Keep the game word conjoin. It is a term in this game.
last: A team can only include each species once. A combined whorl consumes both of its species. Therefore, if you combine a species, you cannot use it individually or in another combined whorl on that same team.

note: Keep the game word tide. It is a term in this game.
last: During a practice battle, press V to open the debug menu. This displays the stats for every whorl and the opponent's last move. You can also modify HP and tides here.

note: The original says the fire is for the old woman's cast, and the rewrite says it is for her leg. Keep the game word cast. It is a term in this game.
last: Come sit by the fire if you want. It's mostly for my leg, though.

note: The original says the bark the Bole drops, and the rewrite says the Bole sheds it, which uses the game term shed.
last: I whittle spoons from the bark the Bole sheds.

note: Keep the name Rider.
last: I collect the discarded parts of Riders. Every single one still ticks.

note: The original talks about casts, and the rewrite turns them into castings.
last: The castings don't fear the cold. They fear the fire.

note: The original says these are Hilt rules (the town), and the rewrite says Hilt is the rule.
last: Hilt is the rule. No crying, no counting out loud, and absolutely no peeking at the bottom.

note: The original says the cards fell with the star, and the rewrite says they fell from the stars.
last: These cards fell from the stars, you know. I merely shuffle them.

note: The original says nothing is held here past the Rim, and the rewrite says everything is free here.
last: Past the Rim. Everything is free here. Mind your hat.

note: The original says grandmother's grandmother, and the rewrite says great-grandmother, which is one generation short.
last: Old Amber's great-grandmother's cast, sitting alongside the others.

note: The original says your whorls are all at level fifty, and the rewrite says you have fifty whorls.
last: Every level is a battle! You've amassed fifty whorls, all of them. // Only conjoined foes are permitted on this floor.

note: The original says Defeat sends you to the bottom, and the rewrite says Defection.
last: Victory means rising one floor higher. Defection means plunging back to the very bottom.

note: The original says the item goes back to the Islander, and the rewrite says it traces back to her.
last: This traces back to the Islander at Cockle Cove.

note: The original choice is Catch it, and the rewrite says Grab it and drops the game term catch.
last: Grab it

note: The original says nothing wild lives here for the Salt Line to keep off, and the rewrite says nothing is here to keep you away.
last: (No wild beasts lurk here to keep you away.)

note: The original says nothing wild lives here to lure, and the rewrite says nothing is here to draw you in.
last: (No wild beasts are here to draw you in.)

note: The original choice is Fight it, and the rewrite says Resist.
last: Resist

note: The original finds a nautilus horn and beach glass, and the rewrite finds a nautilus shell tangled in beach glass. Keep the game word horn. It is a term in this game.
last: A nautilus shell, tangled in seaweed and beach glass, rolled on the sandbar in the inlet.

note: The original hint says to wake one, and the rewrite says don't wake one.
last: Big ones sleep anywhere. I'd bet they're sleeping on my chair. Don't wake one.

note: The original says the Step is a stone, and the rewrite says only It's a stone and loses which item it means.
last: It's a stone. Heavy. It's located beneath the long stones south of Tusk.

note: The original places the Step (the stone) in front of the door, and the rewrite tells the player to stand there.
last: The door faced the water. Stand in front of the door. // The gate is at the end of the path, toward the water.

note: The original choice is Catch it, and the rewrite says Grab it and drops the game term catch.
last: Grab it

note: The original says Ouro gets the kettle, and the rewrite says Ouro puts the kettle on.
last: Ouro puts the kettle on.

note: The original says she does not ask what he is counting, and the rewrite says she does not ask why.
last: He logs you every night. {n} so far, he says. I don't ask what for.

note: The rewrite adds ahead of schedule, so the question what of and the answer everything no longer fit.
last: He's counting the fractures now. Says they're ahead of schedule. I asked what of. // He said everything.

note: The original dusts the shells so the shells know someone still lives there, and the rewrite says so people know.
last: Oh, the basket? Shells. I dust each one so people know someone still lives here.

note: The original says the boat shed (molted), and the rewrite says the old man lost his boat shed.
last: I lost my boat shed last year. Now I own two boats and no sea.

note: The original says the second boat is the first boat's cast, and the rewrite says its reflection. Keep the game word cast. It is a term in this game.
last: That one is the boat. That one is its reflection. I row both of them on Sundays. Across the floor.

note: The rewrite capitalizes the Shallows as a place name, and the original means any shallow water.
last: The Shallows come up to here on you. Three hands. Deep water, no stilt's tall enough. Not even mine.

note: Keep the words written in capitals exactly as they are.
last: FORTY YEARS OF HOLDING MY BREATH IN SPIRE. SO TODAY I'M SHOUTING THE GROCERY LIST. EGGS.

note: Keep the words written in capitals exactly as they are.
last: THREE WHORLS AND A ROARING VOICE. THIS IS THE ONLY PLACE I CAN HAVE BOTH. SORRY.

note: The original says big old whorls sleep in the kelp, and the rewrite calls them coiled shells. Keep the game word whorl. It is a term in this game.
last: Massive, coiled shells slumbered among the kelp forests, // remaining undisturbed unless a jingle broke the silence.

note: The original says the jars of rain are going nowhere, and the rewrite says the seller is not going anywhere.
last: The rain's falling everywhere now. These are the last of the upward-falling jars. // I'm not going anywhere.

note: The original says the rain was caught by the trunk, and the rewrite says a crane's trunk.
last: Jars of rain that goes up. Caught by the crane's trunk. One hundred and twenty per jar. // They're heading up.

note: The original says the smith sells notions for finishing, and the rewrite says finishing touches.
last: Finishing touches. A blade shard keeps a low one low. Clang.

note: The original says nobody crosses, and the rewrite says no one attempts that again.
last: First: you managed to cross. Second: the stones remain stationary now. // Third: no one attempts that again.

note: The original says haul stones (objects) stop a roll, and the rewrite says hauling stones will halt it.
last: First: the gate lies past the holes. Second: hauling stones will halt a roll. // Third: if you walk away, everything rolls back into place.

note: Keep every direction exactly as the original says it.
last: Near the southern path, a bead of star glass is fused to a larger, loose piece.

note: The original says the brook rolls the stones back if you walk off, and the rewrite says you walk off the edge and the brook carries you away.
last: Mess it up and you'll walk off the edge, the brook will carry you away. // Someone ought to prevent that.

note: The original says the wheel came off on a rib bone, and the rewrite says on Rib (the town).
last: A wheel came off on Rib. There are rib bones all over this place.

note: The original says the rain went up and took the hat with it. The rewrite says the rain picked up, which loses the upward rain.
last: The rain picked up again this morning.

note: The original says the auk slides better than the speaker. The rewrite has the speaker claim to slide better than the listener.
last: I slide better than you do.

note: The rewrite pastes the speaker label Smith's boy into the spoken text.
last: Smith's boy: I've got plenty of character now.

note: The original sign says Fall is to the south. The rewrite drops the town and says the fields slope south. Keep the name Fall.
last: The crater fields slope south. Everything here rolls that way.

note: The original is the shell a hole left behind. The rewrite reverses it into a hole left by a shell.
last: A hole left by a shell. It takes stone from what it hits and keeps it. Three cowries. Count your walls afterward.

note: The original says the whorl ate part of the shop counter. The rewrite says it took the speaker's change.
last: The white underside of a forest. It spreads. It feeds. It has taken some of my change. Three cowries, minus the change.

note: The original says the speaker does not ask questions and charges extra for asking. The rewrite says the speaker makes no demands, which loses the point.
last: The husk of an old orchard, shedding fruit. Actual fruit. I have eaten some. I make no demands. Four cowries, plus the cost of asking.

note: The original says it makes your team go round quicker, a speed hint. The rewrite says it makes your world spin faster.
last: The Riders' conception of the heavens. It circles. It makes your world spin faster. Six cowries, which is cheap for a sky.

note: The original says this is a wolf's cast. The rewrite reads cast as a verb and says it is like a wolf casting. Keep the game word cast. It is a term in this game.
last: Like a wolf casting, nose to the ground, chasing a scent from years ago. It sniffs the four cowries before you can offer them.

note: The rewrite invents a buoy register that is active, which reads as nonsense and drops that the whorl came off a buoy.
last: The marsh-mouth buoy register is active. It signals trouble, which is constant. Three cowries. It's ringing now.

note: The original names Tack, a person. The rewrite reads the name as an ordinary word with The tack's cast.

note: This is a page of the guide for young readers. Use short sentences and simple, everyday words.
last: ATK determines the power of physical attacks.

note: This is a page of the guide for young readers. Use short sentences and simple, everyday words.
last: MGK determines the power of magic attacks.

note: This is a page of the guide for young readers. Use short sentences and simple, everyday words. Keep the game word whorl. It is a term in this game.
last: AGI represents speed. Whorls with higher AGI get more turns.

note: This is a page of the guide for young readers. Use short sentences and simple, everyday words.
last: CHA helps a horn catch whorls. It also reduces the wait time after using a Switch. Some moves also utilize CHA.

note: This is a page of the guide for young readers. Use short sentences and simple, everyday words.
last: Each species has unique strengths. One species might have higher ATK, while another has higher DEF. Species also differ in their moves, habits, and types.

note: This is a page of the guide for young readers. Use short sentences and simple, everyday words.
last: Every species receives the same total number of stat points, but they are distributed differently. For example, a fast species will have lower DEF, while a tough species may get fewer turns. A conjoined whorl receives half its points from each of the two original whorls.

note: This is a page of the guide for young readers. Use short sentences and simple, everyday words.
last: This image displays the stats of your lead. Stats increase when a whorl levels up, and certain items you find later can boost them slightly.

note: This is a page of the guide for young readers. Use short sentences and simple, everyday words.
last: HP represents health. A whorl with 0 HP is knocked out. Max HP is the highest HP it can have.

note: The rewrite names the menu option Make leader, and the menu option is Make lead. Keep the game word lead. It is a term in this game.
last: Press X to open the menu, select Team, choose a whorl, then pick Make leader.

note: This is a page of the guide for young readers. Use short sentences and simple, everyday words. Keep the game word whorl. It is a term in this game.
last: DEF helps most against physical creatures. RES helps most against magical ones.

note: Keep the game word whorl. It is a term in this game.
last: In battle, a creature waits after acting. AGI shortens this wait. So a faster creature gets more turns.

note: Keep the game word whorl. It is a term in this game.
last: Example: Your creature has 69 AGI. The foe has 51. Over the battle, yours gets about 9 turns for every 8 the foe gets.

note: Keep the game word whorl. It is a term in this game.
last: Actions resolve in order. The creature whose turn comes first goes first. The top line indicates who moves first.

note: Keep the game word whorl. It is a term in this game.
last: Guess the foe's move. If a big hit is coming, Guard. If the foe Guards, use a dash. If they use TIDE, switch to a creature resistant to it.

note: Keep the game word whorl. It is a term in this game.
last: Sometimes one side moves much sooner. That side picks alone and moves. So a fast creature can move twice before a slow one moves once. The top line shows when this happens.

note: Keep the game word whorl. It is a term in this game.
last: Some actions have short waits. A creature waits 80% as long after Guard as after Attack. The incoming creature waits about 70%. More CHA shortens this wait. The Switch list shows the wait for each creature.

note: Keep the game word whorl. It is a term in this game.
last: Slow 1 pushes the creature's next turn back. It waits 30% of a turn more. Slow 2 does this for its next 2 turns.

note: Keep the game word whorl. It is a term in this game.
last: A wind-up move lands later. A ! appears over the creature while winding up. The top line shows how many moves you get first.

note: This is a page of the guide for young readers. Use short sentences and simple, everyday words.
last: Press X for stats. Go to Team, select the whorl, and choose Look.

note: The original says to switch to a whorl that takes less damage from the move, and the rewrite says one that drains less stamina.
last: You can also switch to a whorl that drains less stamina. An Unstoppable wind-up cannot be interrupted.

note: The original says Guard stops a larger share of a projectile, and the rewrite says it blocks more projectile attacks.
last: Guard blocks more projectile attacks but does not block dash attacks at all.

note: The original says a habit that works after an Attack still works once per Attack, and the rewrite calls these persistent habits. Keep the name Attack.
last: Attacks can hit multiple times. Persistent habits apply once per attack. Habits specifying "hits" apply per hit.

note: The original says a move of the whorl's own type hits harder, and the rewrite says Whorl-type moves as if whorl were a type. Keep the game word whorl. It is a term in this game.
last: Whorl-type moves hit 20% harder. Squall is TIDE. Its TIDE moves hit 20% harder.

note: Keep the game word crest. It is a term in this game.
last: Crests have cooldowns, just like other moves.

note: Keep the name Attack.
last: Plain Attacks have no type. Status effects also lack a type.

note: Keep the game word wind-up. It is a term in this game.
last: Stun: The whorl skips its next turn. Stun also interrupts wind-ups.

note: The original says the whorl is Seen through its next turn after Untouchable ends, and the rewrite says it is revealed at the start of that turn.
last: Untouchable. The whorl takes no damage. Applying another instance of Untouchable does not extend its duration. Once Untouchable expires, the whorl is revealed at the start of its next turn. Until then, it cannot gain Hidden or become Untouchable again.

note: The rewrite says a switching whorl sheds its statuses, which uses the game term shed for dropping a status.
last: Upon switching out, a whorl sheds most status effects. Burn, Bleed, Poison, Rot, Doom, Ward, Regen, and Hidden persist.

note: Keep the game word whorl. It is a term in this game.
last: Marks are indicators applied by certain moves. Each species has unique marks. For example, Kivishi gains a Stone stack each time it is hit.

note: The rewrite replaces the Hidden entry with a Revealed entry and drops what Hidden does. Keep the name Guard. Keep the game word Guard. It is a term in this game.
last: Revealed: The whorl shows next turn after Hidden ends. While Revealed, it cannot become Hidden or Untouchable.

note: The original says Run always works, and the rewrite says only that you can always choose Run. Keep the game word whorl. It is a term in this game.
last: When fighting a wild creature, you can always choose to Run.

note: Keep the game word grotto, nacre, whorl. It is a term in this game.
last: At a shop, select Nacre to apply it to a creature. Each layer adds the same number of points to any stat, strengthening weak stats just as effectively as strong ones.

note: Keep the game word whorl. It is a term in this game.
last: XP needs rise per level. Level 5 requires 72 XP to reach 6.

note: This is a page of the guide for young readers. Use short sentences and simple, everyday words.
last: In round {#1}, each out whorl loses 5% of its max HP. In round {#2}, it loses 10%. The percentage increases by 5% per round.

last: Spend cowries on horns, accessories, and usable items. Conjoining costs cowries, and a cart ride costs 10.

last: Starborn whorls have the same stats as their standard counterparts. Only their appearance differs.

last: Grab retrieves the stone held by the claw. Turning rotates the arm. A polisher buffs the stone. A setter joins two stones. A splitter separates them.
